new_statements.rule_in_words: Two-tone language (H/L lexical; Mid and Falling grammatical). Stress, with slight lengthening, falls on the first syllable of the word stem; noun-class suffixes are never stressed. Stated for the whole Mba group of four languages (Mba, Ndunga, 'Dongo, Ma), hedged ('seems to').
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the statement is hedged ('seems to fall') and applies to the group as a whole, based on Tucker & Hackett field notes plus Carrington 1949 (Mba) and de Boeck 1952 (Ndunga).
new_statements.domain_note: Word stem (root-initial syllable), affixes excluded; group-level generalisation over four languages, not a Dongo-specific analysis; no citation-form or phrase-level discussion visible in the retrieved text.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is a group-level generalisation in Tucker & Bryan 1966 over the four Mba (Class) languages MBA ('Kimanga', mbaa1245), NDUNGA ('Mondunga', ndun1249), 'DONGO (dong1290) and MA ('Amadi'), based on Tucker & Hackett's L.S.N.B.B. field notes plus Carrington 1949 (Mba) and de Boeck 1952 (Ndunga); it is not a Dongo-specific analysis. Same sentence already serves mbaa1245. Dongo = 'Dongo-ko / Dhongoko / Donga, Haut-Uele, DRC.
